title: Your partner is one pawn away from a line
description: In the placing stage of Navakankari, your partner has two pawns in a line with the third point empty, and it is your turn. The video looks one turn ahead, sees that the partner would make a line of three and remove a pawn, and blocks the empty point. Keeko doubts this and wants to start a line of its own.
teaching_notes: One idea: a line of three lets a player remove a pawn, so an almost complete line must be blocked first. Watch for children who chase their own line and ignore the danger.

source: Your partner has two pawns in a line with the third point em
video_script.why: The child knows the rules of Navakankari and now plans a move by thinking one turn ahead.
video_script.substitution: Picture the partner's next move before choosing your own.
video_script.anchor: a Navakankari board from the book, with your partner's two pawns in a line and the third point empty
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko places a pawn far away to start a line of its own. The partner then fills the empty point, makes a line of three and removes one of Keeko's pawns.
video_script.payoff_line: Place your pawn on the empty point to block the line.

final_answer.value: Place your pawn on the empty point to block the line of three
final_answer.spoken: place your pawn on the empty point to block the line

hold_back: your pawn on the empty point
maths_rules: a line of three pawns of one colour lets that player remove one of the other player's pawns that is not in a line
each point holds at most one pawn
partner has two pawns in a line with the third point empty; if it stays empty, partner fills it next turn and makes a line of three
placing your pawn on that point means the line can never be completed there
video_script.design: One idea: look one turn ahead and block. Wrong idea: chase your own line. The board stays as anchor; the doubt comes at the end with Keeko.
